item.stem:
Farhan starts with a full bottle. He pours out $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the bottle, then pours out $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of what remains.

Which claim correctly tracks the amounts?

options.A: After the first pour, $\dfrac{3}{4}$ remains; $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of that remaining is $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the bottle, so $\dfrac{1}{2}$ of the bottle is left.
options.B: He pours $\dfrac{1}{4}$ and then $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the original bottle, so $\dfrac{7}{12}$ is poured in total.
options.C: The second pour uses $\dfrac{1}{3}$ of the original, and that step creates the remaining $\dfrac{3}{4}$.
options.D: The two pour fractions multiply to make the remaining amount, so the bottle ends with $\dfrac{1}{4}\times\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{1}{12}$.
